mainEntity.name: What is the difference between low-voltage and line-voltage outdoor lighting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low-voltage outdoor lighting operates on 12-24 volts, requiring a transformer to reduce standard household current. It is generally safer, easier to install, and more flexible for landscape applications, offering a wide range of fixture options. Line-voltage lighting uses the full 120-volt household current and is typically used for powerful security lights or wall-mounted fixtures that cover larger areas. While line-voltage offers greater light output, it requires more complex installation and adherence to stricter electrical codes. We primarily focus on low-voltage systems for aesthetic landscape illumination.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low-voltage lighting uses 12-24V with a transformer, safer and easier for landscapes. Line-voltage uses 120V for high-output needs, requiring complex installation.
